stories.story: As a returning shopper, I want my saved address pre-filled at checkout so that I can pay without retyping it.
stories.acceptance:
Given a signed-in shopper with a saved address
When they open checkout
Then the address fields are pre-filled and remain editable

Given a signed-in shopper with no saved address
When they open checkout
Then the fields are empty and no error is shown

stories.story: As a shopper, I want the whole checkout on one page so that I can see every step before committing.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper with items in the cart
When they open checkout
Then address, delivery, payment and summary are visible on one page without navigation

Given a section is incomplete
When the shopper tries to pay
Then the first incomplete section is focused and names what is missing
stories.notes: Layout shell only; payment lands in S02.

stories.story: As a first-time shopper, I want to check out without an account so that I am not forced to register.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper who is not signed in
When they open checkout
Then they can enter an email and continue as a guest

Given a guest completes an order
When the confirmation is shown
Then they are offered account creation with the order already attached

stories.story: As a shopper, I want to pay by card so that I can complete my order.
stories.acceptance:
Given a valid test card and a complete address
When the shopper submits payment
Then the order is created and the confirmation page shows the order number

Given the provider returns success
When the webhook arrives
Then the order moves to Paid exactly once, even if the webhook is delivered twice
stories.notes: Provider test mode and published test card numbers only.

stories.story: As a shopper whose card is declined, I want to be told clearly and keep my basket so that I can try another card.
stories.acceptance:
Given a card that the provider declines
When the shopper submits payment
Then a plain-language message names the problem and the basket and address are preserved

Given the provider times out
When no response arrives within the timeout
Then the shopper sees a retry option and no duplicate order is created

stories.story: As a shopper, I want tax and shipping itemised before I pay so that the total holds no surprises.
stories.acceptance:
Given a basket with a delivery address
When the summary renders
Then goods, shipping and tax are listed separately and sum to the displayed total

Given the address changes to another tax jurisdiction
When the shopper updates it
Then tax and total recalculate before payment is enabled

stories.story: As a shopper, I want to enter a promo code so that an advertised discount is applied.
stories.acceptance:
Given a valid, in-date promo code
When the shopper applies it
Then the discount line appears and the total drops accordingly

Given an expired or unknown code
When the shopper applies it
Then the code is rejected with a reason and the total is unchanged

stories.story: As an overseas shopper, I want prices in my own currency so that I know what I am paying.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper in a supported non-home currency
When checkout renders
Then all amounts show in that currency with the rate's as-of timestamp

Given the rate is older than the staleness window
When checkout renders
Then the home currency is shown instead and the event is logged

stories.story: As a shopper, I want my address checked as I type so that delivery does not fail.
stories.acceptance:
Given a partial address
When the shopper pauses typing
Then provider suggestions appear and one can be selected to fill the fields

Given the validation provider is unavailable
When the shopper submits
Then the typed address is accepted and flagged for manual review

stories.story: As a product manager, I want checkout funnel events so that I can see where shoppers drop out.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper moves through checkout
When each step is reached, completed or abandoned
Then a named event with the step and order value is emitted once

Given analytics is blocked by the browser
When events fail to send
Then checkout continues without error

stories.story: As a shopper on a phone, I want checkout usable at mobile width so that I can order on my phone.
stories.acceptance:
Given a 375px viewport
When checkout renders
Then there is no horizontal scroll and every control is reachable with one thumb

Given the on-screen keyboard opens
When a field is focused
Then that field stays visible above the keyboard

stories.story: As a shopper using a keyboard or screen reader, I want to complete checkout unaided so that the service is usable for me.
stories.acceptance:
Given keyboard-only navigation
When the shopper tabs through checkout
Then focus order follows the visual order and focus is always visible

Given a screen reader
When a validation error appears
Then it is announced and programmatically tied to its field
stories.notes: WCAG 2.2 AA on the checkout flow; the wider audit is INI-11.

stories.story: As the team, I want the new checkout behind a flag so that we can roll it back without a deploy.
stories.acceptance:
Given the flag is off
When a shopper opens checkout
Then the legacy checkout is served

Given the flag is on for a percentage of traffic
When it is switched off
Then new sessions fall back to legacy within one minute and in-flight orders still complete

stories.story: As the team, we want the monolith's billing read and write paths mapped so that extraction order is known.
stories.acceptance:
Given the monolith codebase and database
When the spike completes
Then every caller of billing tables is listed with read/write intent and traffic volume

Given the map exists
When the team reviews it
Then the extraction order and the dual-write boundary are agreed and written down
stories.notes: Time-boxed spike. Re-estimate the rest of the epic on its findings.

stories.story: As the team, we want a deployable billing service skeleton so that later stories have somewhere to land.
stories.acceptance:
Given the service repository
When CI runs on main
Then it builds, tests, and deploys to staging with a passing health check

Given the service is deployed
When /health is called
Then it reports version and database connectivity

stories.story: As an internal consumer, I want invoices readable from the billing service so that I can stop querying the monolith.
stories.acceptance:
Given an invoice that exists in the monolith database
When it is fetched from the billing service API
Then the payload matches the monolith's for every field in the contract

Given an unknown invoice id
When it is fetched
Then the service returns 404 with a machine-readable error

stories.story: As the team, we want invoice writes dual-written behind a flag so that we can verify the new store under real traffic.
stories.acceptance:
Given the dual-write flag is on
When an invoice is created in the monolith
Then it is written to both stores and a mismatch raises an alert

Given the billing service is unavailable
When an invoice is created
Then the monolith write still succeeds and the missed write is queued for replay

stories.story: As the team, we want historical invoices backfilled and reconciled so that the new store is complete.
stories.acceptance:
Given the backfill job runs to completion
When the reconciliation report is produced
Then row counts and checksums match per month, and any mismatch is listed by invoice id

Given the job is interrupted
When it is restarted
Then it resumes without duplicating rows

stories.story: As an internal consumer, I want invoice reads served by the billing service so that the monolith stops being the source.
stories.acceptance:
Given the read-cutover flag is on
When any consumer reads an invoice
Then the billing service serves it and p99 latency stays within the agreed budget

Given error rate exceeds the threshold
When the cutover is active
Then traffic reverts to the monolith automatically and the team is paged

stories.story: As the team, we want the monolith's invoice endpoints retired so that there is one source of truth.
stories.acceptance:
Given no caller has used a monolith invoice endpoint for the agreed observation window
When the endpoints are removed
Then the build passes and no consumer errors appear in the following 24 hours

Given a forgotten caller appears
When it calls the removed endpoint
Then it receives 410 Gone with the replacement URL

stories.story: As a subscriber, I want renewals processed by the billing service so that billing no longer depends on the monolith scheduler.
stories.acceptance:
Given a subscription due for renewal
When the billing service job runs
Then exactly one renewal invoice is raised and the payment is attempted once

Given the job runs twice for the same period
When the second run executes
Then it is idempotent and raises no second invoice

stories.story: As a developer, I want the worst flaky tests identified and quarantined so that red builds mean something again.
stories.acceptance:
Given 30 days of CI history
When the flake report runs
Then the 20 highest-flake tests are ranked by failure rate and quarantined from the blocking suite

Given a test is quarantined
When it fails
Then the build still passes and the failure is recorded against its ticket

stories.story: As a developer, I want time-dependent test failures fixed so that the suite passes regardless of when it runs.
stories.acceptance:
Given tests that depend on the current clock, timezone or date boundaries
When they are run with the clock set to a month end, a DST change and a leap day
Then they pass in every case

Given the fixed tests
When run 50 times in CI
Then there are no failures

stories.story: As a developer, I want order-dependent test failures fixed so that tests can run in parallel.
stories.acceptance:
Given tests that share fixtures or global state
When the suite runs in randomised order and in parallel
Then every test passes

Given a test leaks state
When the suite runs
Then the leak is caught by a teardown assertion rather than by a later test failing

stories.story: As a team, we want new flakes caught at the gate so that the backlog does not refill.
stories.acceptance:
Given a dashboard of flake rate by test and by suite
When a newly added test fails intermittently across 20 CI runs
Then it is flagged on the dashboard and the owning team is notified

Given a pull request adds a test that flakes in pre-merge runs
When the gate evaluates it
Then the merge is blocked with the evidence

stories.story: As an on-call engineer, I want a current rotation and escalation runbook so that I know what to do at 3am.
stories.acceptance:
Given the rotation is published
When an alert fires outside working hours
Then the paged engineer and the escalation path after 15 minutes are unambiguous

Given a new joiner takes their first shift
When they follow the runbook
Then they can acknowledge, triage and escalate without asking anyone

stories.story: As an engineering manager, I want a P1 bug SLA dashboard so that breaches are visible before they are complaints.
stories.acceptance:
Given open P1 bugs
When the dashboard refreshes
Then time-to-acknowledge and time-to-fix are shown against the SLA with breaches highlighted

Given a P1 is raised
When the acknowledge target is 30 minutes from being missed
Then the owning team is notified

stories.story: As a customer, I want the standing P1 backlog cleared so that long-broken things get fixed.
stories.acceptance:
Given the P1 bugs open at the start of the sprint
When the sprint ends
Then each is fixed, reclassified with a written reason, or closed as not reproducible

Given a fix ships
When it is verified in production
Then the originating report is updated and closed

stories.story: As an on-call engineer, I want the noisiest alerts fixed or muted so that pages mean something.
stories.acceptance:
Given 30 days of alert history
When the top five noisiest alerts are reviewed
Then each is either made actionable, re-thresholded, or deleted with a reason recorded

Given the changes are live
When the next week's pages are counted
Then out-of-hours pages have fallen against the previous week

stories.story: As a security owner, I want dependencies and patches current so that known vulnerabilities are not left open.
stories.acceptance:
Given the dependency scanner report
When the sweep completes
Then no critical or high advisory older than the agreed window remains unaddressed

Given a patch cannot be applied
When it is deferred
Then the reason, the compensating control and a review date are recorded

stories.story: As a support engineer, I want the most repeated manual request automated so that toil stops growing.
stories.acceptance:
Given the support request log for the quarter
When the most frequent manual request is automated as self-service
Then a requester can complete it without engineering involvement

Given the automation fails
When it errors
Then the requester sees a clear message and the old manual path still works

stories.story: As a service owner, I want SLOs and error-budget alerts so that reliability is measured, not asserted.
stories.acceptance:
Given the agreed SLIs for availability and latency
When the error budget burn rate exceeds the fast-burn threshold
Then the owning team is alerted with the contributing endpoints

Given a month closes
When the SLO report is produced
Then budget consumed and remaining are stated per service

stories.story: As a support engineer, I want handoff docs for the new billing service so that I can support it without the authors.
stories.acceptance:
Given the billing service is serving reads
When support receives a billing question
Then the runbook names the dashboards, the common failure modes and their first-line remedies

Given an unfamiliar error
When support follows the escalation section
Then the owning team and the required diagnostic bundle are named

stories.story: As a compliance owner, I want a quarterly access review so that access matches current roles.
stories.acceptance:
Given the access list for production systems
When the review completes
Then every entitlement is confirmed by the system owner or removed, and the evidence is retained

Given a leaver is found with live access
When the review runs
Then access is revoked the same day and the gap is recorded

stories.story: As a team, we want incident retro actions closed so that the same incident does not recur.
stories.acceptance:
Given the retro actions raised this quarter
When the sprint ends
Then each is done or has a named owner and a date, with none silently dropped

Given an action is overdue by more than one sprint
When the review runs
Then it is escalated to the manager with the risk restated
